Understanding Psoriasis

A comprehensive overview of psoriasis — its causes, symptoms, types, and the latest advances in therapeutic management.

Overview

What is Psoriasis?

Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune disorder that accelerates the lifecycle of skin cells, causing inflammation, redness, scaling, and irritation. The condition affects millions of individuals worldwide and can significantly impact physical, emotional, and social well-being.

Unlike temporary skin conditions, psoriasis is driven by immune system dysfunction that triggers excessive skin cell production. Although the exact cause remains complex, genetics, environmental factors, infections, stress, and immune abnormalities all contribute to disease progression.

The condition is characterized by periods of flares and remission, and its severity ranges from mild — with small patches — to severe, covering large areas of the body. Psoriasis can also affect the joints, leading to a form called psoriatic arthritis.

Signs & Symptoms

Common Symptoms

Symptoms can vary depending on the type and severity of the condition. People living with psoriasis may experience any combination of the following.

Red, inflamed patches of skin with a well-defined border
Thick silvery-white scales overlying raised plaques
Persistent itching, burning sensation, and soreness
Dry or cracked skin that may bleed
Swollen, stiff joints in cases of psoriatic arthritis
Thickened, pitted, or ridged nails
Emotional distress, anxiety, and reduced quality of life
Cyclic flares and remission patterns
Skin lesions in sensitive areas (scalp, genitals, folds)
Classification

Types of Psoriasis

Psoriasis presents in several distinct clinical forms, each with unique characteristics, distribution patterns, and treatment considerations.

01

Plaque Psoriasis

The most common form, affecting approximately 80–90% of patients. Characterized by raised, inflamed red lesions covered with silvery-white scales. Plaques typically appear on elbows, knees, scalp, and lower back.

02

Guttate Psoriasis

Presents as small, drop-shaped lesions (2–10mm) scattered across the trunk, arms, and legs. Often triggered by bacterial infections, particularly streptococcal throat infections, especially in children and young adults.

03

Inverse Psoriasis

Appears in body folds such as the armpits, groin, under the breasts, and around the genitals. Presents as smooth, red, inflamed patches rather than scaly plaques. Friction and sweating can aggravate symptoms.

04

Pustular Psoriasis

A severe form involving white pustules (blisters of non-infectious pus) surrounded by red, inflamed skin. Can be localized to the palms and soles (palmoplantar) or widespread across the body (generalized).

05

Erythrodermic Psoriasis

A rare but potentially life-threatening form that affects large portions of the body simultaneously with widespread inflammation and exfoliation. Requires urgent medical attention and hospitalization in severe cases.

06

Psoriatic Arthritis

A chronic inflammatory arthritis affecting up to 30% of psoriasis patients. Causes pain, swelling, and stiffness in joints along with skin symptoms. Can lead to permanent joint damage if left untreated.

Therapeutic Management

Treatment Approaches

Modern psoriasis management has been transformed by advances in immunology and molecular biology. Treatment selection depends on disease severity, affected body areas, patient history, and comorbidities.

At AlsysLife, we are dedicated to discovering innovative therapeutic solutions capable of improving long-term patient outcomes and restoring confidence to individuals living with chronic inflammatory skin diseases.

Our research into natural product-derived biologics and small molecule inhibitors targets the specific immune pathways responsible for psoriasis, aiming to deliver first-in-class therapies with superior safety profiles.
